ruling.RULING-6: A lane binding is only real if the lane can RUN on it, and only the run proves it. After the reboot the Codex toolchain pin named a binary the in-place upgrade had removed, so all three lanes were fail-closed dead: the independent acceptance officer could not run, and no amount of config inspection would have said so. The repair had to move two surfaces together (the live declaration and the registry's expected values) because the drift gate compares them, and it had to be proved by a live probe with a nonce and a usage receipt, not by a green config test. The same round also produced the mirror lesson for prose: the pool's per-lane selection_note was a hand-written declaration of a machine-checked field, it had gone stale, and no automated gate had flagged it because prose is not a machine-checked field. Generated declarations beat maintained ones.

The R7 reproducible-build work was carried to candidate commit b6eee02 and MERGED as PR #3 (merge commit 590c2adf6563af6ef98ea9a7125ddb9d40977c17). Along the way the hosted CI had been RED for five consecutive runs on both ubuntu and windows while the maker's Windows suite was green. The cause was reproduced locally rather than guessed: the CI runner installs pytest and nothing else, so the `build` package is absent there, and the sdist-normalisation test stubbed the build COMMAND but still let build() resolve a backend interpreter, so it raised SystemExit -- an environment gap reported as a product failure, which then took the mutation probe down with it. build() now takes the builder interpreter as an argument and resolves it only when the caller has not supplied one; a new regression test pins that the resolver is not consulted at all in the stubbed path, and the write-through invariant test skips when git is absent instead of raising. Measured in a CI-equivalent environment (git present, no build backend): 206 passed, 4 skipped, exit 0; on the hosted runners: all four checks success.

The R7 checker round 4 (arm openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol, nonce R7CHK-NC-20261021-A4, 237 s) produced a real, complete, INCONCLUSIVE -- NOT ACCEPTED verdict. Its sandbox forbids every filesystem write, so it could not run the two-build comparison, the full pytest run, the mutation experiments or the W3 write-through experiment; it did not attempt prohibited mutations and did not adopt the maker's receipt as independent evidence. It still found three real product defects, all now fixed: D1 a failed build became a SkipTest on ANY nonzero exit, D2 the W1 regression test accepted either boolean result so it asserted nothing, D3 the mutation probe treated any nonzero pytest exit as a caught mutation so an infrastructure error could pose as a kill.
